I will keep it simple and do what I know best on the North China Plain: I will grow winter wheat and then summer maize on the same land. In Quzhou County, this is the most familiar and steady way for me to use the whole year, and at my age I would rather follow a system I understand well than take risks with crops that need more labor, more marketing trouble, or more technical skill. I will use improved seed, not the cheapest old seed, because I want better emergence and more stable yield. I will plough before wheat so the soil holds water better and the straw can be mixed in, and after wheat harvest I will use rotary tillage for maize so I can plant quickly. I will apply fertilizer in a moderate way, with more nitrogen for maize and enough phosphorus for rooting, and some potassium to support grain filling and stress tolerance. I will irrigate wheat more because it needs support through winter recovery, jointing, and grain filling, while maize will get fewer waterings unless rainfall is too low. I will not spray many times, only enough to control the main diseases, weeds, and insects, because too many sprays cost money. My goal is stable grain production, manageable fieldwork, and reliable output from the land.
